What we improved in make-motion, and how to use it

Versions 1.3.0 and 1.4.0: eleven upgrades, each with a clip rendered from one JSON file

Date
2026-11-02
Version
portable-artifacts 1.4.0
Status
Measured numbers from the repo

The verdict

make-motion now times, grades and maps a video

Good

You can now ask for cuts on the beat, a set loudness, graded photos, Lottie animations, maps, a bar chart race, text behind a person and WebGL transitions. Each clip below came from one motion.json.

  • Sound: beat-anchored times and a two-pass loudness stage (-14 LUFS in viral mode, any target with a flag).
  • Picture: colour grades, Lottie, maps, a race chart, 13 new blocks (28 in all), cutouts and 2 WebGL transitions.
  • Workflow: click an element in the preview to name it, and approve a storyboard for clips over 20 s.

The promo

One JSON file made this vertical promo#

Beats

Cuts and cues can land on the beat#

A keyframe time, cue or audio start can now be "beat:<n>". beats.mjs finds the beat grid of a music file with a local detector, so a retimed track keeps its cuts on the beat. Before, times were plain seconds.

Loudness

One flag sets the loudness of the mix#

render.mjs --loudness <lufs> runs a two-pass loudnorm after the encode, with --true-peak <dbtp> as the ceiling. Viral renders now do it with no flag, at -14 LUFS and -1 dBTP. A spec with no target renders as before.

Colour grades

Photos and clips take a colour grade#

image and video elements take a grade: a preset (warm, cool, mono or film) plus optional exposure, contrast and saturation. It is one SVG filter, and check.mjs judges text contrast on the graded pixels.

Lottie

Lottie animations play inside a video#

A lottie element plays a Lottie JSON file offline through lottie-web 5.13.0, frame by frame, so renders stay deterministic. Keyframes move, scale or fade the whole animation; speed (0.25 to 4) and offset retime it.

Maps

Maps highlight places and draw arcs#

Bundled atlases (world-110m, world-50m, us-states-10m, us-counties-10m) work as chart data with no network. Two blocks use them: map-highlight lights named countries or states, and flow-map draws labelled arcs between longitude and latitude pairs.

Bar chart race

A bar chart race is one block#

The race block turns 4 to 200 rows of period, name and value into ranked bars that swap places, with counters. top sets how many bars show (3 to 10) and periodSeconds how long each period lasts. The scene must last at least periods times periodSeconds.

Nine more blocks

Nine more blocks cover common screens#

comparison-split, before-after, notification-stack, chat-thread, timeline, testimonial, lower-third-tag, lower-third-social and lower-third-ticker join the set. Each lays itself out for 16:9 and 9:16, takes theme colours and keeps clear of the caption zone.

Cutouts

Text can sit behind a person#

cutout.mjs cuts a person out of a photo (PNG) or a clip (WebM with alpha) on this machine with MODNet. The text-behind-subject block then puts big text between the picture and the cutout. The weights are checked against a SHA-256 before every use.

WebGL transitions

Two shader transitions join the cuts#

A scene's transition can now be gl-ripple (a wave through both scenes) or gl-cube (a box turning in perspective, from any of four edges). A render captures both scenes and blends them with a shader in software WebGL.

Click to pick

Click an element to name it exactly#

In the live preview, clicking an element copies its spec path and id, for example scenes[1].elements[3] id=title, and shows a 2 s toast. Paste that into your request and the agent edits that element instead of guessing from your wording.

Storyboard

Long clips get a storyboard to approve#

For a clip over 20 s, storyboard.mjs writes a make-explainer plan page: a summary, one timeline event per scene, a theme decision, an approval and a question. You answer on the page; the agent reads the answers only through answers.mjs, then writes the spec.

How to start

Install once, then ask for a clip#

Example prompts

Three prompts to try first#

  • A vertical promo

    viral mode

    /make-motion a 9:16 Reels promo with a voiceover: a hook, a bar chart race, a cube transition and a soft call to action.

  • Cut to music

    beats

    /make-motion an 8 s square clip cut to data/loop.wav: the title on beat 1, a pulse on every beat.

  • Text behind a person

    cutout

    /make-motion a 6 s clip with PRESENTING in giant letters behind the person in speaker.jpg.

Before upgrading

Five changes alter what an upgrade does#

From the 1.3.0 and 1.4.0 entries in CHANGELOG.md.
ChangeWhat happensWhat to do
Viral renders are normalised1.2.0 only reported the mix against -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP; now a two-pass loudnorm runs and the line reads on target.Add --loudness off to skip it. It needs ffmpeg 5.1 or later.
New pinned dependencieslottie-web 5.13.0, world-atlas 2.0.2, us-atlas 3.0.1 (npm audit: 0 vulnerabilities).Run npm ci; the Licences table in README.md lists each.
Cutout and voiceover installs keep each other (1.4.1)Both are on-demand npm install --no-save, so npm prunes what an install leaves off its command line. Before 1.4.1 each install deleted the other.Now each --fix names its own pin plus the one already installed, so both stay. npm ci still removes both: rerun --fix kokoro and --fix cutout.
The on-demand audit script fails on a bad pinscripts/audit-on-demand-deps.sh now audits KOKORO_PIN and CUTOUT_PIN and exits 1 if either fails.Check any CI step that calls it.
Specs without a GL transition or cutout are unchangedSame bytes at --fps 10 --size 320x180 with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1793318400: q3-revenue cb304e5d..., ok-crossfade ac068343... (one machine).Nothing.

Not proven yet

Several claims rest on small samples#

AreaWhat is measuredWhat is not proven
Beat detectionA synthetic 120 BPM loop (0.88 confidence) and the repo's beats tests.Real music. The detector can read half or double tempo; some genres are listed as known misreads.
WebGL transitionsComposed-frame hashes of three transitions (ripple, cube left, cube down) equal on Ubuntu, macOS and a local Mac.Windows, other directions or sizes, and equal MP4 bytes across platforms (they differ).
LoudnessOne synthetic loop at -16, and the promo mix (voice and cues, no music) at -14.0 LUFS and -2.4 dBTP against a -14 target.Mixes with real music, and ffmpeg older than 5.1.
EvalsA Haiku model wrote valid specs for 28 of 28 Gate 3 prompts and 2 of 2 Phase 4 prompts. Only 8 of the 16 Gate 3 items passed validate on the first call; the rest were fixed within the run.Other models and other hosts.
CutoutsOne pre-cut portrait in the clips; the eval prompt was valid on the first build.Cutout quality across varied photos. Open follow-ups: the cutout cache is never pruned, a huge PNG is size-checked late.
Pick and storyboardTests and the Gate 3 review.A recorded real session: the clip here is a mock-up.
Open follow-upsListed under Gate 3 and Phase 4 in the plan's Status.Fixes for notification-stack stagger, flow-map on a US map, a race size cap, and captions drawn into GL transition shots.
